> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5d872fbfe2b3f11ccaac09f9a536484ca2f4fd69` — the merge of head `e321fc54f209cbba4d1ea74fcb8639ea8e027a42` into base `39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d872fbfe2b3f11ccaac09f9a536484ca2f4fd69 && git checkout 5d872fbfe2b3f11ccaac09f9a536484ca2f4fd69
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243 e321fc54f209cbba4d1ea74fcb8639ea8e027a42 && git checkout -B drift-repro 39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243 && git merge --no-ff e321fc54f209cbba4d1ea74fcb8639ea8e027a42

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39ca58787acbadd3b6e28810e2baa8576bd0d243` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e321fc54f209cbba4d1ea74fcb8639ea8e027a42`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/object-value-shape.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/run-door-input-shape.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/field-error-code-catalog.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-trigger-params-shape.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts (the `type: 'flow'` arm, line 579, the builder's second caller), packages/runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts (`readActivationBody`, line 232: the `deps.error` + `VALIDATION_FAILED_STATUS` + `validationFailureDetails(validationFailure(...))` precedent the action door now copies), packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts (`splitSemanticCode` / `buildApiError`, the promotion of `details.code` into `error.code`), packages/runtime/src/validation-failure.ts and packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts (the constructor and the 400 constant), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`FieldErrorCode`, `invalid_type`) and packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (`VALIDATION_FAILED`), packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/package.json and packages/runtime/tsup.config.ts (the package's public entry), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs (`DISPATCHER_DOMAIN_DIR`, `discoverDomains`, the NOT-DECLARED refusal, the `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` table), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`findMigrationPrescription`, `readDisposition`), .github/workflows/lint.yml (which job runs which gate), .changeset/25821-trigger-params-object.md (the sibling's prose face), docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md, docs/adr/0114-field-level-error-code-catalog.md, .changeset/25976-run-door-input-shape.md (prose face, read for ②)

Inputs: card #25976 body and its three comments (triage 6411002575, claim 6411222289, os-dev-report 6413120939); the sibling card's contract review 6410594343 and PR #25974 (body, file list; its merged code is what `main` carries at `05f7758f`); PR #26034 body, file list (7 paths) and the net diff against `main` at this head (`Accept: application/vnd.github.diff`, 659 lines); the check-runs on the head, read twice (at open and at write time). Read-only: the diff, the local checkout at `main` and the gate scripts were read; nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated.

### ① Derived judgments

**CI on the head at write time.** 46 check-runs: 29 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 6 `in_progress` (Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 of 8), 0 failed, 0 cancelled. Concluded green: Build Core, Test Core 5/8 and 8/8, every Lint job (ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI/release & engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lanes, tooling self-tests, `Lint & Repo Gates`), every Type Check job (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, TypeScript Type Check), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected, and the four card/branch/single-writer guards. The judgments below are read from the code; the six open shards are the dev's reported local run (runtime typecheck + test, 453 files / 7399 passed / 19 skipped at `e321fc54`) until they conclude.

**a. The action door: which inputs are now refused, with what answer — right.** `actions.ts` lines 688-713 (head) replace two truthy-object reads. The body: `objectValueFailure('(body)', body ?? {})` refuses a string (`""` included), a number (`0` included), a boolean (`false` included) and an array (`[]` included); `undefined` and a JSON `null` body become `{}` through `?? {}` before the check and keep the bodyless call. Before the diff, every one of those refused shapes was replaced by `{}` and the action ran (an array passed `typeof` and read as a body with no `recordId` and no `params`). The `params` key: `objectValueFailure('params', reqBody.params)` refuses a string, number, boolean, array and an explicit `null`; `undefined` (key absent) and any non-null non-array object, `{}` included, are admitted, and `reqParams = reqBody.params ?? {}` builds the bag an object `params` always built. Before, `null`/`0`/`false`/`""`/a string became `{}` and ran, and an array was handed on AS the bag. The answer is `deps.error(message, VALIDATION_FAILED_STATUS, validationFailureDetails(validationFailure(message, [failure])))`: `details` carries `{ code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', fields: [{ field, code: 'invalid_type', message }] }`, and `buildApiError` (`error-envelope.ts` line 118) promotes that `details.code` into `error.code` with `httpStatus: 400`, so the wire reads `400` / `error.code === 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` / `error.details.fields[0] = { field: '(body)' | 'params', code: 'invalid_type', message: 'expected an object (a map of names to values), received ...' }`. It is the exact spelling `activation-gate.ts` line 232 already uses for `readActivationBody`, so the action door's refusal rides the envelope the census test already pins for that door. Position: the hunk sits immediately after the flow-action 503 probe (line 684-686 on `main`) and before `enforceActionParams`, `loadActionSubjectRecord` and dispatch, which is where the PR body says it sits; a refused call reads no row and asks neither the automation service nor the script registry. The new suite pins `execute` and `executeAction` not called on every refused shape (9 `params` shapes x 3 actions, 8 body shapes x 2 actions) and pins the five accepted bodies (`{params:{note:'x'}}`, `{params:{}}`, `{}`, `undefined`, `null`) reaching both engines with the bag they always carried.

**b. The trigger doors' body — right, and reaches exactly the wire doors.** `buildAutomationContext` (`automation.ts` line 156) now reads `objectValueFailure('(body)', body ?? {})` before `ctxBody` is typed, throwing `validationFailure('Invalid trigger body — ...', [failure])`. Refused: a string, number, boolean, array (`""`, `0`, `false`, `[]` included); admitted: `undefined`, `null` (both become `{}`) and any plain object. Before, a string/number/boolean body became `{}` and dispatched the flow with an empty bag, and an array passed `typeof` and reached the flat-body branch, which forwarded its indices as params. I confirmed the caller set on `main` by grep: exactly two production call sites, `respondToFlowTrigger` (`automation.ts` line 2172, reached by `POST /:name/trigger` at line 3024 and the legacy `POST /trigger/:name` at line 2821) and `executeFlow` in `endpoint-executor.ts` line 579 (every declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint). No flow-to-flow node, scheduler or MCP path builds through it, so the body refusal cannot over-reach a non-wire caller. The throw is the same `validationFailure` the #25821 `params` refusal throws two lines below, on the same ride the sibling review 6410594343 traced to `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` + `details.fields` at both dispatcher exits and `endpointErrorAnswer`; the 404 (`flowIsUnknown`) and 403 (`flowStartRefusal`) gates run before the builder at both call sites and are untouched by this diff. The suite pins both REST routes x 8 refused shapes with `execute` not called, both routes x 3 bodyless shapes (`undefined`, `null`, `{}`) dispatching with `params: {}`, and the declared endpoint through the real `executeEndpointTarget` (8 refused, 1 accepted).

**c. The resume door: no observable change beyond the declared one — right.** `const rawBody = body ?? {}` (line 3306 on `main`) is unchanged context, so the value handed to the check is never `undefined` and never `null`. On that domain the old predicate `typeof rawBody !== 'object' || Array.isArray(rawBody)` and `objectValueFailure`'s `value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)` are the same truth table: a string, number, boolean and array refused, every plain object admitted, the bodyless resume kept. The top-level message is byte-identical: the new `expected` argument supplies `an object with ${accepted}` and the formatter appends `, received ${received}` with the same words the arm-local `jsonTypeOf` produced (`null` / `an array` / `a ${typeof}`). The one wire change is `fields[0].message`, which gains the `, received ...` suffix; `field` and `code` are unchanged, and the changeset declares it ("the resume door's `fields[]` message now also names the type received"). `jsonTypeOf` at line 3320 is still used by the `branchLabel` refusal (line 3419 on `main`), so the hoist leaves no dead local; ESLint concluded green.

**d. No error code is minted.** The top-level code is `VALIDATION_FAILED` (error-code-ledger.zod.ts line 302, in the standard list) and the field code is `invalid_type` (errors.zod.ts line 247, `FieldErrorCode`, ADR-0114); both are the codes the resume door and the #25821 refusal already emit. Nothing here is `Clause-②: yes`. The census test gains four rows for the two new emission sites, which is what ADR-0114's catalog test asks of a new `fields[]` emitter.

**e. Public surface: unchanged.** `packages/runtime/package.json` exports `"."` only, resolving to `dist/index.*`; `tsup.config.ts` has the single entry `src/index.ts`; `src/index.ts` does not export `object-value-shape.js` (grep over the barrel: no hit). `objectValueFailure` was a module-private function in `automation.ts` on `main` and is now a named export of a module no barrel re-exports, so the published `.d.ts` is identical before and after. No `packages/spec/**` path is touched; the claim's constraint holds. The MCP `run_action` door (`action-execution.ts`) is outside the diff and unchanged, as the acceptance note says.

**f. Tests.** The new suite drives the real `HttpDispatcher` and the real `executeEndpointTarget`, pins both directions at all three doors, and pins the three doors' `fields[0]` rows side by side with the resume sentence byte-for-byte. The PR records red-first (78 failed / 59 passed on base) and three single-anchor ablations each reproducing a red (17 / 36 / 33). I did not re-run them (read-only); the assertions as written would fail on the base code at every refused shape, which is the property the counts claim.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25976-run-door-input-shape.md`: `'@objectstack/runtime': patch`, title `fix(runtime)!: ...`, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — ...`, line-initial `Metadata-protocol: none (...)`, exactly one `adr-0087:` marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a BREAKING banner with Before / Now / Fix. The PR body carries the same two lines at line start (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). Measured against the diff: the only published change is a runtime accept-set narrowing at three request doors; no spec key, authorable value, stored shape or export moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind, and under AGENTS.md's level rule (`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition) `patch` is the right level. The marker's exemption holds on the gate's own test: `findMigrationPrescription` fires on a FROM/TO placeholder, an arrow rewrite under migration framing, a framed or header-framed rewrite table, or a framed removal; the changeset's `**Fix.**` line is a prose sentence with none of those, and the body has no migration heading, no arrow and no table, so `no-migration-prescription` is not self-contradicted. The disposition text is the sibling's (25821) word for word with the doors widened, and that changeset merged through the same gates. Note for the seat: `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` runs for real only in `cut-rc.yml` (lint.yml runs its `--self-test` half under `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`), so on PR CI the marker is judged by reading; I have. Check Changeset concluded `success` on this head. The `(narrowing)` arm is what makes this record owed, and `no (narrowing)` is the measured value, departing from the claim's bare `no` exactly as the dispatch order asked. Convention check: `no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch` + BREAKING + `not-required` — all four present on the changeset, the two lines present on the PR body. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`** in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- **a. Declared departure 1 — the action door's whole BODY, fixed in place.** Judged as the brief asks. Same defect class: the body read `body && typeof body === 'object' ? body : {}` on `main` line 688 is the identical truthy-object coercion as the `params` read one line below it, on the same door, starting the same run with an empty bag; the card's business reason ("a caller that sends a wrongly shaped request still starts a run with no inputs") names it even though the card's Measured section probed only `params`. Mechanical: one more call of the same function with the same envelope, eleven lines in a file the claim's surface already holds. Declared with evidence: the PR body's "Departure from the claim's wording, declared" section, the live probe (`"oops"`, `[1,2]`, `42` as the body each `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` at `(body)`, the control runs listing only the controls), 16 refusal cases plus the census row in the tests, and the changeset's `Clause-②` line and Before / Now / Fix both name the body. Because it widens the narrowing beyond the card's literal "Wanted", it had to be on the published carrier, and it is. Accepted.
- **b. Declared departure 2 — `packages/runtime/src/object-value-shape.ts`, outside `packages/runtime/src/domains/**`.** The gate rule exists as the dev states it: `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` line 962 `DISPATCHER_DOMAIN_DIR = 'packages/runtime/src/domains'`, `discoverDomains()` (line 2283) lists every `.ts` there that is not `.d.ts`, `.test.` or `.conformance.`, and lines 2565-2575 red any name absent from `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` with "NOT DECLARED. Add it to DISPATCHER_DOMAINS". The alternative — declaring the helper in that table with `handBuilt: 0`, as `activation-gate.ts` is — exists but would be a false row: the table's own rationale for `activation-gate.ts` is that it answers refusals through `deps.error`, whereas this module writes no response at all and audits as nothing. So one sibling file beside `validation-failure.ts` in `packages/runtime/src/`, imported relatively by both domains, with no barrel export and no gate-table edit, is the minimal placement. The gate's job (`Lint · docs & code guards`, which runs `pnpm check:route-envelope` at lint.yml line 2814) concluded `success` on this head. The path is outside the claim's declared surface but inside the package and the lane, declared in the PR body's Acceptance notes and in the report. Accepted.
- **c. The dev's `Clause-②` departure from the claim's bare `no`.** The measured value is right (② above); the claim said the dev measures and declares. Accepted.
- **d. Out-of-scope finding, main-red dogfood battery.** `test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` reds on `handleI18nRequest` control count 3 vs 4; `domains/i18n.ts` is not in this PR's file list, and the dev's reading that `origin/main` carries 4 occurrences since the ETag change is consistent with the #25785 ratchet note in `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` (`i18n.ts` went to `handBuilt: 1` for the ETag/304 face). Not this diff. The CI `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head is `success` (it is not the full battery). To the seat: file it as its own card against the census file, with the dev's dedupe strings.
- **e. Out-of-scope note, MCP `run_action`.** The same truthy-object guard in `action-execution.ts` is unreachable behind the tool's input schema (`-32602` measured). Noted, not a card; agreed.
- **f. Docs drift.** Six hand-written pages are flagged through the `invalid_type` literal. I read `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` and `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx` for the two doors: neither restates the old coercion of a trigger body or an action `params` (the only matches are the resume door's own `invalid_type` prose and the `patch`-row text about declarative updates), so no page is falsified by this diff. Advisory only.
- **g. Check-runs not success/skipped.** Six `in_progress` at write time: Test Core 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 4/8, 6/8, 7/8. None failed. Under the Tier S rule the seat lands only once they conclude green beside this record; this record judges the code and does not wait on them.
